title: Genre conventions
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:16Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank's convention cards focus on deliberately subverting or preferring genres rather than on the basic expected features of a genre (clues and suspects, invented worlds and magic) that this Year 8 point needs, so no existing point teaches the same idea at the right depth.

draft.title: Genre conventions
card: A genre is a type of story, such as mystery, fantasy or science fiction. Stories in the same genre share familiar features called conventions.
a puzzle to solve, with clues, suspects and a detective or other character who hunts for the truth.
an invented world, often with magic, strange creatures and a struggle between good and evil.
imagined science or technology, such as space travel or robots, often set in the future or on other planets.
draft.remember: Conventions are the features readers expect from a genre, and they help us recognise it.

a.q: Which feature is a convention of the mystery genre?
opts: A set of clues that point to a suspect
A kingdom ruled by a magical dragon
A spaceship travelling to a distant planet
A robot that learns to feel emotions
a.why: Clues and suspects are the puzzle at the heart of a mystery. The dragon belongs to fantasy, and the spaceship and robot belong to science fiction.
a.clue: Think about what a detective needs to solve a case.

b.q: Kiri is reading a story set in a world with floating islands, a wizard school and spells. Which genre is it most likely to be?
b.why: An invented world with magic and spells are conventions of fantasy. Science fiction relies on imagined science or technology, not magic, so it is the tempting wrong choice.
b.clue: Look for an invented world and magic.

a.best: A set of clues that point to a suspect
